summaries.demographer: James Lee is a 21-year-old never-married white male living with his parents and younger sister in Paso Robles, California (Q51, Q84, Q88, Q89). He has a high school diploma and some college coursework but is not currently enrolled, placing him in a transitional education-to-work stage (Q90, Q91, Q92). He is not currently in the workforce, though he has prior part-time cafe and informal event experience (Q16, Q65, Q72). His household appears stable and middle-class, with parents owning the home and carrying main expenses while James contributes intermittently (Q55, Q58, Q83).
summaries.behavioral_economist: James's choices show present social rewards balanced against emerging long-term planning: he values group activities, local events, and travel, but is increasingly attentive to savings, benefits, and career stability (Q61, Q62, Q83). He is risk-aware rather than risk-averse, avoiding unnecessary school debt while trying to build a hospitality career through lower-cost local experience (Q02, Q108). Peer comparison affects his emotions and motivation, especially when friends graduate or move into stable jobs (Q43, Q83). His main behavioral friction is procrastination on paperwork and applications, which he recognizes as a barrier to converting social skill into income (Q04, Q17, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: James is a no-party-preference Independent who leans Democratic and describes himself as center-left, practical, and locally focused (Q24, Q95, Q96). His civic concerns center on housing affordability, water use, climate, tourism, and environmental stewardship in San Luis Obispo County (Q23, Q24, Q25). He votes by mail and is still developing consistent local-election habits, using voter guides and trusted people while trying not to simply copy his parents (Q23). On race and policing, he reports moderate impact from Black Lives Matter, with increased awareness, some discussion, and limited protest participation (Q26, Q29, Q30).
summaries.psychologist: James presents as extraverted, affiliative, and identity-driven by community, hospitality, and shared experiences (Q01, Q07, Q109). His emotional regulation relies heavily on movement, social contact, cooking, and outdoor activity, while uncertainty can trigger anxiety, comparison, procrastination, and caffeine overuse (Q43, Q45, Q50). He has no diagnosed depression or anxiety disorder, but he is self-aware about stress patterns and open to therapy if symptoms worsened (Q45). His self-concept blends charisma and usefulness with a desire to become more reliable and independent, especially around career follow-through (Q65, Q83, Q108).
